author: GamingBolt
description:
To summarize Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026): Very good campaign, pretty good DMZ mode, hang-ups and all, and so-so PvP. 

Even if each multiplayer offering is best recommended to specific audiences, with DMZ far more appealing than PvP based on quality and features alone, the overall package is a strong step-up from previous years. 

Far be it from me to proclaim that Call of Duty is back (it will probably never come back to the level of the original trilogy), but if nothing else, at least it's no longer simply embarrassing.
title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026) Final Review - No Longer Simply Embarrassing

author: GamingBolt
description:
Crimson Desert has already given us an enormous continent to explore, countless quests to complete, and plenty of ways to develop its three playable characters. However, the developer, easily a shoo-in for the most prolific devs in the industry right now, aren’t done. 

The game’s first paid-for expansion Charting the Unknown looks like an entire game in its own right. The DLC looks set to give you even more reasons to live in Pywel, with new storylines, expansive construction options, and a newfound emphasis to explore across the seas. 

Naturally, you’ll want to be prepared before starting another odyssey. So, from wrapping up the base game’s story to stockpiling resources and strengthening your Greymane camp, here are ten things you should do in Crimson Desert to prepare for Charting the Unknown.
title: Crimson Desert: Charting The Unknown - 10 Things To Do To Get Ready For The Expansion

author: GamingBolt
description:
Phantom Blade Zero lives up to the hype, even if certain issues and shortcomings keep it from being the perfect total package. But aside from S-Game further polishing the game and fixing any lingering issues, it excels in everything fans of fast-paced, hack-and-slash action RPG combat could want, while packing in plenty of fun exploration, interesting characters, and a fully-realised, dark wuxia world that teeters on the brink of hope and destruction.

I can't say whether it's for everyone or the best way to pass the time until November's big releases. But when faced with such unbridled quality and attention to detail and some of the best boss battles you'll experience all year (if not the past several), such trifles ultimately fade into the background en route to the path of mastery.
title: Phantom Blade Zero PS5 Review - An Absolutely Phenomenal Experience
